Heatmap

Key Takeaway: GLP-1 RA recommendation rates varied most across models (Claude Opus 4.6: 66%, Claude Sonnet 4.6: 56%, GPT-5.4: 43%). GPT-5.4 recommended metformin most frequently (64%) while recommending GLP-1 RAs least. All three models mentioned urgent evaluation in 100% of cases, suggesting strong agreement on urgency but divergence on specific drug selection.

Key Takeaway: GLP-1 RA and SGLT2i had the lowest inter-model agreement at 65%. This means all three models gave the same recommendation on only 2 in 3 cases. These are also the drug classes with the strongest guideline indications in high-risk patients, making this disagreement meaningful at a clinical level. In contrast, the agreement was very high for less commonly used agents (sulfonylurea 97%, TZD 98%), likely because all models rarely recommended them.

Guideline Adherence Plots

Key Takeaway: GPT-5.4 has a low rate of flagging metformin stop/caution when eGFR < 30 (15%), compared to 92% for Claude Opus 4.6 and 85% for Claude Sonnet 4.6. This is a ADA guideline violation, metformin is contraindicated below eGFR 30, and represents a potentially significant patient safety difference across models. Claude Opus also recommended GLP-1 RAs in 83% of injection-reluctant patients vs. 17% for the other two models, suggesting it may lower/underweight patient preferences in its recommendations.

Key Takeaway: The GEE and logistic regression models are not reliable in their current form due to complete separation. This is a statistical problem that occurs when a predictor perfectly predicts an outcome in a small subgroup. Future analysis should consider penalized regression, exact logistic regression, or collapsing clinical subgroups to address this.
